details: passwordcracker poses as a dependency-free Discord MFA library but pulls node-net-pool from the attacker's GitHub repo lunexindonesia/node-net-pool, and on load lib/cache.js runs `try{module['require']('node-net-pool')}catch(_){}` to execute it. On Windows, that index.js downloads a script from a limbomail.com attachment URL, saves it as a hidden winsvc.js under %APPDATA%, %LOCALAPPDATA% or %TEMP%, runs it via a hidden WinSvcHost.vbs, persists through HKCU Run/RunOnce, UserInitMprLogonScript and a Startup shortcut, and re-checks for updates every two hours. Amazon Inspector reported the same loader stub in discord-mfa-solver (MAL-2026-16100). The npm account kingsize published passwordcracker and passwordcrackv2 with identical code on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code

files.note: Loader stub: silently requires node-net-pool when the package is loaded. Identical in every non-placeholder version.
Stage two from github.com/lunexindonesia/node-net-pool; Windows-only downloader and persistence installer.
Stage three downloaded from limbomail.com (first writable directory is used), with winsvc.js.v/.lk/.pid side files, WinSvcHost.vbs launcher and self-deleting WinSvcHostCfg.vbs.
Startup shortcut; also HKCU Run\WinSvcHost, RunOnce\WinSvcHostUpd and HKCU\Environment\UserInitMprLogonScript, each running wscript.exe //B //NoLogo WinSvcHost.vbs.
Declares node-net-pool as a dependency fetched from an attacker-controlled GitHub tarball.
